retrospective.harder_than_needed: This story's own charter (deletions + docs only, zero new correctness logic) collided with a real dependency it didn't anticipate: extending the AC-BOUND-3 scanner to guard the outbox IDB key (deliverable 5) immediately tripped false positives in three files outside stories.json's literal scope.includes (publish-outbox.ts, marmot-adapter.ts, publish-outbox.test.ts), because that scanner does raw text matching with no comment/string stripping (unlike bound-4's scanner). Landing the deliverable as specified required rewording doc comments and swapping two inlined template-literal keys for the already-exported outboxKey() helper in files never named in scope.includes -- a real, unavoidable scope-boundary tension between the task brief's explicit ask and stories.json's coarser-grained scope declaration, resolved by treating the detailed task brief as authoritative (per its own explicit instruction) and keeping every such edit behavior-preserving (proven by an unchanged, fully-green 1017-test run). The bound-4.structural.test.ts ALLOWLISTED_LEGACY_FILES judgment call (keep vs. delete task-reducer.ts) also took real analysis: the deliverable's own check ('is applyEvent/comparator imported by any production path?') answers NO, which reads like license to delete, but task-reducer.test.ts's ~40 mutation-pinned test cases have no proven equivalent-behavior replacement (task-crdt.test.ts covers only the tie-break comparator, not applyEvent's per-event-type field-copy semantics) -- deleting it would have risked violating AC-MIG-4's 'no test file deleted without a same-behavior replacement' bar under a deletions-only story's limited license to independently verify that equivalence. Kept the file and documented the rationale in the allowlist comment instead.
retrospective.surprised_by: The S9-authored isEngineReadPathEnabled() JSDoc already fully anticipated this exact story and documented itself as vestigial, unreferenced, and left specifically for S13 to delete -- confirming the flag was not load-bearing (the task brief's STOP condition) required almost no investigation, since S12 had already made shouldMountEngine flag-independent and left an explicit paper trail saying so.
